title: Party Organizations and Complementary Political Control,
title_zh: 党组织与互补性政治控制
source: Journal of the European Economic Association
abstract: Abstract We study how political parties engage in political targeting of resources by coordinating politicians across multiple levels of government. We combine thousands of election outcomes from the Indian state of West Bengal with 300 million payments from a welfare scheme jointly controlled by state and local governments. We show that the state government gives disproportionate funding to co-partisan local councils, which target payments to raise votes for national candidates. Welfare payments are diverted to reward local councilors who successfully deliver votes, and to recruit opposition councilors. The ruling party recruits candidates only where it lacks a majority, systematically expanding its control.
abstract_zh: 我们研究了政党如何通过协调多级政府中的政治家来实施政治资源定向。我们将印度西孟加拉邦数千个选举结果与一项由邦政府和地方政府共同控制的福利计划中3亿笔支付记录相结合。研究显示，邦政府向同党地方议会提供不成比例的资金，这些资金被用于定向支付以提升国家层面候选人的得票率。福利支付被挪用，用于奖励成功拉票的地方议员，并招募反对党议员。执政党仅在未获得多数席位的地方招募候选人，从而系统性地扩大其控制范围。
